items.front: Founder of the Reddi kingdom (1325), and his first capital?
items.back: Prolaya Vema Reddi; first capital Addanki (Panta Reddi clan).

items.front: The hill-fort capital most associated with the Reddis?
items.back: Kondavidu (Kondaveedu Fort, Guntur), to which Anavota Reddi shifted the seat.

items.front: The Reddis first rose as subordinates of which lineage?
items.back: The Musunuri Nayakas — part of the post-Kakatiya Telugu warrior resurgence.
1325–1448 CE, over coastal & central Andhra and Rayalaseema.

items.front: The second Reddi branch on the Godavari (est. 1395)?
items.back: The Rajahmundry (Rajamahendravaram) branch — Kataya Vema, Allada Reddi, Virabhadra Reddi.

items.front: Third of the Telugu Kavitraya, court poet of Prolaya Vema; completed which work?
items.back: Errapragada (Errana); completed the Aranya Parva of the Andhra Mahabharatam; titled Prabandha Parameswara.

items.front: Court poet of Peda Komati Vema Reddy titled 'Kavi Sarvabhauma'?
items.back: Srinatha — wrote Sringara Naishadhamu, Bhimakhandamu, Kasikhandamu, Palnati Vira Charitra; honoured with Kanakabhishekam.

items.front: Scholar-king (r.c.1386–1402) who authored a dance treatise?

items.back: Repaired Srisailam Mallikarjuna steps, patronised Ahobilam Narasimha; titled Apratima-Bhudana-Parasurama.

items.front: How did the Reddi kingdom end?
items.back: Kondavidu annexed by Vijayanagara (1424); Rajahmundry taken by the Gajapatis (c.1448).

items.front: Historical significance of the Reddis after 1323?
items.back: Led the Hindu political revival in Andhra following the fall of the Kakatiyas.

items.front: Gajapati founder who pressed on coastal Andhra, and his capital?
items.back: Kapilendra Deva (1434), capital Kataka (Cuttack); 'Gajapati' was one of the four royal titles.
Dharmasutra-based rule, one-sixth land tax, and Motupalli sea-port trade.
